newsitem.title: USA: Ritz-Carlton pulls out of 4 hotels, files lawsuit.
newsitem.headline: Ritz-Carlton pulls out of 4 hotels, files lawsuit.

text.p: The Ritz-Carlton name has vanished from hotels in New York, Washington, Houston and Aspen, Colo., following the abrupt termination Saturday of the relationship between Ritz-Carlton Hotel Co LLC and Sheikh Abdul Aziz Bin Ibrahim al Ibrahim, the owner of the hotels.

Ritz-Carlton LLC, which bestows the tony name on the hotels it is hired to run, said over the weekend it had concluded 2-1/2 years of disputes with the sheikh's holding company by pulling out of the hotels and filing a lawsuit in federal court in New York.

"We've taken down the flags and severed our operating agreements with the owner," Karon Cullen, a spokesperson for the hotel company, said Sunday. "It's unprecedented. We've never had to take this kind of action before. It's really sad."

Ritz-Carlton said the owners, Al Anwa USA Inc, a holding company controlled by al Ibrahim, owed more than $4 million in back pay and fees to the management company, had meddled in the management of the properties and refused to make improvements.
No one at the holding company could be reached for comment over the weekend.
"They have constantly interfered with our operating decisions. We tried to settle the problems and tried to resolve them, and it was just becoming intractable," Cullen said in telephone interview.

The complaint, filed in U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York, names the defendants as N.Y. Overnight Partners LP, D.C. Overnight Partners LP, Savanah Limited Partnership and New Remington Partners, as well as an escrow agent.
